# Bounded complex128 array execution and resource accounting

The private `emc._array_backend` selects NumPy or optional CUDA/JAX for the
material facade. [Consumer configuration](usage-current-interface.md) remains
separate from the [physical certification policy](numerical-control.md).
Readers and fresh reverse-mesh/finite-angle oracles stay CPU; no backend
selection can mint or bypass a certificate.

## Contraction and residency

For each channel, flatten pair/final-band indices into states. Each state's
external-band outer product is conjugate(g_a) times g_b. Frequency-dependent
retarded factors multiply this state-by-external-matrix array via batched
matrix products. This avoids a pair-by-K-by-frequency-by-band-by-band
intermediate. Stream at most16 pairs per channel; bound frequency factors
at512 points. Prepare device inputs once per batch and reuse across eta
cases. `device_get` synchronizes output before host accumulation/validation.
Complex128/float64 is mandatory; NumPy use never imports JAX.

Full-matrix Dyson inversion returns the anti-Hermitian spectral matrix,
not entrywise imaginary parts. The2048-frequency reduction chunks retain
unchanged PSD, causality and physical spin-projector observations. Analytic
zero-energy values and derivatives use the same state outer products;
single-pair NumPy primitives remain independent numerical references.

## Failure transitions

A rejected tile removes included pair digests/reports and decrements their
certificate counters. Excluded zero modes have coverage but no reports;
rollback must not pop nonexistent certificates. Shrinking the tile must
shrink the allocated Sigma workspace, not merely change loop bounds.
Certification failure still discards the entire scientific group.

Magnon public exchange/reference arrays are mutable. Cache-free J(0)
recomputation avoids a stale diagonal term after moment/Q/axis/JR changes;
vectorized Fourier calculation is retained.

## Resource evidence

The case-buffer planner includes channel list/stack overlap, outer products,
frequency factors and host/device overlap. It is not a total-RSS bound:
imports, JIT/compiler buffers and allocator history are process observations.
CUDA allocator statistics and host VmHWM have distinct scopes.

Linux ru_maxrss can retain pre-exec high-water history; executable-scoped
`/proc/self/status` VmHWM resets across exec. A difference between those
metrics is not evidence of a kernel defect or a subtractable constant.
The fallback native unit is KiB on Linux, bytes on Darwin. Stream JSON to
avoid constructing the complete serialized string or deep-copying large
case evidence. Historical numerical bundles remain immutable.

See the [performance evidence](../subprojects/fe-spectrum-performance-and-gpu-acceleration/specs/research/2026-10-04-jax-gpu-performance.md)
for measured scope, precision decisions and missed performance targets.

## Post-P3b optimization feasibility

Real four-K component profiles distinguish regular q6 (contraction
dominant) from half q6 (certified-pair/orbital work dominant). Exact-zero
contraction-row pruning measured approximately 1.8x on a genuine absorption
batch, with Sigma differences below 7e-16; timings vary and this is not
a full-envelope speedup. Use actual zero weights/vertices, never sorted
band parity or numerical thresholds. The finite-angle orbital memo is
currently per K-block stream, not global to a q group.

Gamma-only and exactly nested-grid Sigma reuse preserve the mathematical
dependency split, but retained-buffer prototypes showed no robust speedup.
Fewer FLOPs alone do not prove a faster execution path. Fresh reverse
native-mesh and covariance checks remain mandatory.

See [post-P3b feasibility evidence](../subprojects/fe-spectrum-performance-and-gpu-acceleration/specs/research/2026-10-07-post-p3b-optimization-feasibility.md)
for profiles, prototype timings, candidate order and unproved limits.

## Implemented exact-zero NumPy pruning

NumpyBatch now retains the union across K of rows with nonzero weighted
occupation and nonzero vertex components, before building outer products.
No cutoff is used. Dense rows, mixed-K activity and arbitrarily small
weights retain the same full-matrix and analytic-derivative contracts.
An empty retained set contracts to correctly shaped zero matrices.

The unchanged 33-case Fe envelope passed with identical certification
coverage and 43 comparison outcomes. All 227 fields match the historical
reference (maximum absolute difference 1.34e-11). Dense-group time measured
1273.87 s versus prior P3b 1432.95 s; driver VmHWM 978.21 MiB. This is
8.43x the historical timing, not the 10x target; single-run timing varies.
Actual absorption-batch preparation/contraction/derivative median improved
0.04823 -> 0.02579 s; outer storage 5,971,968 -> 2,840,832 bytes.
See the [implementation record](../specs/quick-tasks/2026-10-07-exact-zero-contraction.md).

## GPU utilization is not end-to-end throughput

An idle-at-launch monitored RTX3090 rerun recorded mean11.4%utilization,
median0%,417/554idle samples and just one external Chrome19MiB sample.
The full complex128 JAX envelope still took2787.09s evaluation and
2374.62MiB driver RSS versus current NumPy1277.59s/978.21MiB. All33cases,
43comparison outcomes and227field equivalence passed. Adaptive tile-level
certificate counts can differ while physical mode/K coverage is preserved.

JaxBatch.add synchronizes/copies each512-frequency result before CPU
accumulation. Certified pair production and validation remain host work.
Low utilization does not establish whether preparation, transfer, compile
or launch overhead dominates; it requires component timings. Utilization
is kernel-active time, not FP64throughput or occupancy. Current NumPy
exact-zero pruning is not implemented in JAX.
See [monitored rerun evidence](../subprojects/fe-spectrum-performance-and-gpu-acceleration/specs/research/2026-10-08-idle-gpu-rerun.md).

## Device-resident flush accumulation (2026-10-11)

`JaxBatch.add` now concatenates its 512-frequency contraction blocks on
the device and performs one `device_get` per flush instead of seven, and
backends declare a `pair_block` (jax 128, numpy keeps the historical 16)
that `_run_block` uses for flush cadence. Arithmetic per block is
unchanged — blocks wrote disjoint frequency slices — so this is a
transfer/launch optimization only. Measured on the five-K probe: flush
cumulative 9.50 -> 6.09 s, wall 52.08 -> 48.96 s; the remaining time is
CPU-side certified-pair production, which dominates small cuts. On the
full 241-K q12 path the optimized GPU run finished in 1495.89 s versus
2339.60 s CPU (1.56x) with 207240/207240 gates passed and equivalence
rel <= 2.5e-14 (traces) / 1.3e-15 (Sigma(0), dSigma(0)). Host driver
VmHWM stays ~2.6 GiB from the JAX import — above the 1 GiB process
target — while the CUDA allocator peaked at 969.58 MB. Single-cut
measurement; not an envelope-wide speedup claim. See the
[GPU task](../specs/quick-tasks/2026-10-11-jax-gpu-q12.md).

### VRAM-sized device batches (2026-10-11)

The JAX flush cadence is no longer fixed: `_sized_pair_block()` budgets
reported free VRAM minus `max(15% limit, 256 MiB)` headroom over a
12 MiB-per-pair estimate, with no arbitrary ceiling. Missing statistics
or room for fewer than 16 pairs refuse CUDA execution rather than force
a batch above budget. `identity()` records the choice. On an idle
RTX 3090 it selects 1281 pairs. The final uncapped q12 path reached
7661.31 MB allocator peak (of 18.97 GB limit), 2720.32 MiB host
VmHWM, 428296/428296 gates; CPU equivalence rel ≤ 1.30e-13
(traces) and ≤ 1.04e-15 (sigma0/dsigma0). Runtime 2183.68 s versus
1574.04 s with a capped 1024 pairs (6057.75 MB allocator peak,
207240 gates) and 1495.89 s at block128. Increasing the staging
flush shrank adaptive K tiles from 17 to 8 and approximately doubled
certified pair work; higher VRAM usage is not faster here. The sizing
model is a launch-time estimate for this Fe workload, not a VRAM
reservation; concurrent processes can consume memory later. The
1 GiB PRD figure is a host-RSS target, not a VRAM budget. See the
[VRAM task](../specs/quick-tasks/2026-10-11-jax-vram-sized-batches.md).


## Group-scoped orbital memo (2026-10-09)

`iter_certified_pairs` optionally accepts a caller-owned content-keyed
orbital memo, and the spectrum facade shares one per frozen q group across
all K tiles and cuts. The finite-angle orbital is K-independent, so builds
drop from modes x tiles to modes per group. Measured on a real q6h group
(864 blocks, 216 modes): 864->216 builds, 50.01s -> 39.54s (repeat39.69s),
certificates identical. Default None keeps per-stream behavior; reverse
proofs and counters are untouched. Order-controlled measurement is
essential: the first evaluation in a process pays one-time staging costs
that can invert an A/B comparison. Not an envelope-wide claim.

## Frozen-preparation reuse (2026-10-09)

ElectronicStates now carries the frozen physical identity (an empty field
falls back to the original digest), the facade shares one
group_preparation tuple (model plus both identity digests) across every
tile and cut of a q group — computed lazily inside cut failure handling —
and the covariance gate reuses each rotated spinor dict for eigenvalues and
the transverse derivative (4 builds instead of 6 per call). Combined with
the memo hoist, a real q6h group went50.74s->35.65s;spinor_hR builds
5212->3473. Published pair digests, certificates and gate counts are
unchanged. Remaining to_wannier_ham volume is dominated by per-pair
covariance gates; sharing those proofs is contract decision B and stays
excluded. See the [task record](../specs/quick-tasks/2026-10-10-preparation-reuse.md).

# Bcc Fe input frame and reference-bias contract

The user supplied `/home/hexu/projects/TB2J_examples/Wannier/` for Story 014.
`bccFe_QE_Wannier90/W90/` contains paired `Fe_up`/`Fe_down` Wannier90
Hamiltonians, centers and input files, with `output_J_k292929/TB2J.pickle`.
`getJ.sh` records the exchange command and the explicit Fermi energy
12.6256 eV. The model has nine s,p,d spatial orbitals, one Fe atom at the
origin, and 597 real-space blocks per spin. QE's input is collinear
`nspin=2`, with starting magnetization -1; the TB2J moment is -2.2322001 muB.

## Frame conversion, not moment absolutization

The supported loader requires +z ferromagnetism. A global pi rotation about
x exchanges electron up/down blocks and rotates the moment by
`diag(1,-1,-1)`. Isotropic J is invariant. Staging must transform both
objects together, preserve real-space degeneracies, and leave all source
files unchanged. The temporary combined spin-major model is then read by
HamiltonIO into its standard interleaved basis. This is not an SOC-spinor
calculation or a general new paired-spin API.

Before modes are computed, validate orbital counts, R ordering, Wigner-Seitz
weights, Hermitian R reversal, up/down cells and atom species, spin-pair
centers, site-local centers, and the matching TB2J cell/site/moment. Separate
spin Wannier centers and common projections do not prove common orbital
gauge; this is an explicit input assumption, not a result of certification.

## Certified model versus first-principles prediction

An initial real-file probe found positive magnon energies along Gamma--H:
0.0310638563, 0.1067232495 and 0.2023355209 eV at path fractions 0.125,
0.25 and 0.5. Gamma remains zero with no boson normalization.
The unchanged adjoint, metric, covariance and finite-angle gates passed.
The option-B reference residual is 1.3700937583 eV in the raw-block
Frobenius norm, relative norm 0.0161090687. This is not an error bound on
observables or a declaration that omitted spin bias is negligible.

Every material-derived caption must say that the site-local option-B
reference discards nonlocal spin-dependent hopping. The Gaussian-window
lambda proxy is not a self-energy slope. Coarse mesh/broadening sweeps are
findings, not convergence certificates. Fe ARPES literature is context only;
no material self-energy or predictive kink agreement is claimed.

## Provenance and exchange-tail limits

The raw source inventory (paired Hamiltonians/centers/win/wout, SCF/NSCF
inputs, exchange pickle/report, generation command and Fe UPF) is stored
under paper `data/bccfe/inputs/{W90,DFT}` with 15 SHA256 hashes. No public
fetchability is claimed. The input repository HEAD predates the generated
exchange output, so that commit is not an immutable pin for the chosen J.
The supplied NC-PBE UPF is `../DFT/pseudo/Fe.jry.pbe.UPF`, SHA256
`371345212f2e0e81bfb97b9562099b39e3901399513a980386643bff2c3270d5`.
The explicit E_F is accepted from the example scripts; no stored QE output
independently verifies it.

All 1242 isotropic J entries are consumed unchanged. Finite hopping support
does not imply finite exchange support: the resolvent Green function can
extend beyond H(R), so cutting J at the 597 electron R blocks is invalid.
The source audit found far-R exchange sensitivity among the supplied
13/19/23/29 k meshes; internal certification does not establish source J
convergence. The separate source biquadratic terms are not included by the
isotropic-bilinear magnon loader.

## Completed material evidence

The full stored-input CLI replay passed 44 certificates / 176 gate reports
in 246.2 s. Its NPZ is byte-identical to the supplied-source calculation,
SHA256 `2b79716063f9e9d7545d4c1cec64079889dd028c0170847e9b2bade68d3d12b9`.
The five PDFs and material macros regenerate byte-identically; the
18-page manuscript builds and all panels were visually inspected.

For k6^3/q3^3 and sigma=0.1 eV, the k-averaged band-summed discrete proxy
is 0.0966080882. At the same k/sigma with q2^3 it is 0.0075791774;
at q3^3 with sigma=0.05/0.2 eV it is 0.0000219211/1.2967241423.
This sensitivity is a finding, not a converged material coupling constant.
The fan uses the strongest sampled path transfer q=H and 12 grouped arrows;
individual degenerate-band entries are not treated as gauge-invariant.

## Later source-validity finding (2026-10-01)

Numerical-control research probed the four raw k13/k19/k23/k29 exchange
sources beyond the original coarse samples. All four have negative
unshifted magnetic quadratic forms at small q on Gamma-H. At reduced
q=(-0.05,0.05,0.05), the k29 form is about -0.001699 eV. Independent
Fourier sums of the raw J values confirm the sign, so this is not an
eigensolver regularization or reader-version artifact.

The full half-offset q6^3 grid also rejects 44/216 q for k13 and 6/216
for each of k19/k23; k29 passes that particular grid but still fails the
small-q path probe. The source files/J/moments are unchanged. The completed
coarse showcase remains a historical sampled-identity demonstration,
not evidence of a globally stable ferromagnetic source. Its archived
NPZ/provenance/figures are not silently rewritten by this finding.

The numerical-control Architecture is approved and its campaign is
implemented. The actual four-source facade run reproduces the veto for all
four models and publishes no spectral metrics. New artifacts and diagnostic
paper panels live under `data/numerical_control`, separate from this archive.
See [full source assessment](../subprojects/numerically-controlled-bcc-fe-emc-benchmark/specs/research/2026-10-01-exchange-source-compatibility.md).

## Additional inputs and band-spectrum comparison scope

The separately stored legacy bccFe_QE_Wannier90/TB2J_results source is not
one of the modern four-source series. It matches the paired electron geometry
and passes q3/q4/q6/half-q6 plus the 0.02 Gamma-H sentinel, with 928 J pairs
and moment -2.25827237 muB. Its TB2J 0.3.5 header lacks the generating k mesh
and contour settings; sampled eligibility is not source convergence or global
stability. Four other newly assessed local candidates fail. These observations
do not amend the four-source veto or the historical showcase.

Raw and option-B sorted band energy sets differ by up to 0.52256 eV on the
sampled high-symmetry path. This reference bias is not an EMC self-energy.
Bare Lorentzian spectral maps are display-broadened bands, not interaction
linewidths or simulated ARPES intensities. The retarded material path now
uses independently checked full-matrix spin-flip channels and causal
physical spin traces; numerical/source convergence remains unestablished.

For bulk LSWT the relevant first experimental target is the low-energy
bulk-derived majority band of Cui et al., DOI 10.1016/j.susc.2007.04.069.
The Fe/W(110) 160-200 meV replica is a surface/optical-film-magnon problem;
the 2019 1.5 eV minority-hole anomaly is predominantly a renormalized-Stoner
channel, not a magnon frequency. Growth temperature must not be relabeled
as measurement temperature. See [primary comparison evidence](../subprojects/bcc-fe-electron-magnon-band-spectra-and-experimental-comparison/specs/research/2026-10-02-bccfe-arpes-comparison.md)
and [raw-source audit](../subprojects/bcc-fe-electron-magnon-band-spectra-and-experimental-comparison/specs/research/2026-10-02-bccfe-magnetic-inputs.md).

## Actual interacting pilot (2026-10-03)

The legacy source completed the approved full-q envelope: 33 case instances
passed physical certification, while all 43 one-axis comparisons were
sensitive. The 121-point source-cell Gamma–H ray has reduced endpoint
(-.5,-.5,-.5), Cartesian −[001], not an assumed nominal [100] cut.
The five-anchor [-12,40] eV audit integrates 17.998109 states/K versus
18 expected; worst per-spin relative residual is 0.035773%, verified only
within the declared finite-window/quadrature criterion.

Evaluation took 10860.9155 s and peaked at 1201.4102 MiB; whole-driver
highwater 1971.5078 MiB includes artifact writing. Both exceed the 1 GiB
process-RSS target and are explicit resource findings. No allocation
component was profiled. The actual 25-page manuscript and six PDFs build;
the seven rendering outputs rerender byte-identically and Fe pages were
visually inspected. Numeric Cui 2007 data was not obtained, so only the
40/270 meV mechanism-separated energy landmarks are shown, cut unmatched.

Four false global-chain completeness reasons were corrected by pure
held-control-family metadata reduction, not new physics. Executed code,
original metadata and correction sources are archived/hash-bound; the
computed NPZ digest stays 05a444ea8db920a00ad786632971dc2441672b3593c08f92d01e476c80c54b38.
All numerical arrays and measured per-link changes remain unchanged.

## Resolved P–Gamma–N pilot spectrum (2026-10-09)

The separate optional Fe path uses the real BCC cell’s ASE special points:
P=(-.25,.25,-.25), Gamma=(0,0,0), N=(0,0,-.5) in reduced coordinates.
The exact Gamma junction is K index132 of241; true Cartesian reciprocal
distance steps are0.01433377–0.01436335 inverse Angstrom. The external
electronic path is not a Brillouin-zone integration mesh; the magnon q6
grid carries the normalized integration weights.

With the unchanged legacy source,2001energies [-4,1]eV at2.5meV spacing,
eta=gamma=10meV and model T=0K, the sole q6 case passed46440/46440gate
reports and produced the full spin-projected spectral maps. Driver VmHWM
was696.6914MiB. Its overall comparison verdict is *unresolved* because a
single case provides no q/eta/gamma convergence chain; this is not a
physical-gate failure. The figure uses option-B bare overlays (nonlocal
spin-dependent hopping discarded) and cannot be compared quantitatively
to ARPES intensity or treated as a finite-temperature prediction. The
historical Gamma–H datasets remain separate.

The subsequent wider P–Gamma–N display requires actual new spectral
evaluation: the old [-4,1] eV array cannot yield [-5,3] eV weights by
replotting. At fixed 2.5 meV step the new grid has 3201 energies. Linear
color normalization suppresses faint visual streaks formerly amplified by
$I^{0.4}$/$I^{0.45}$ power maps without discarding any weights. The
ARPES-inspired palette over the complete window includes unoccupied
$E>E_F$ calculated states, so it must not be described as occupied-only
photoemission. This is a display decision, not a new convergence or
experimental-intensity certificate. The original bundle remains archived;
see [wide-window task](../specs/quick-tasks/2026-10-10-fe-pgn-wide-low-contrast.md).

The actual independent widened run passed 53320/53320 physical gate
reports with no failures and an unresolved one-case overall verdict;
its NPZ SHA256 is
`0488f65e184fa8c837faba4e0459c36133476311667553d79f5db6fbf3650e91`.
This attests the chosen controls and gates, not magnon-grid, broadening
or source convergence.

The owner subsequently chose an intermediate display exponent
$I^{0.7}$ across production and A/B/C/D, rather than the linear $I^1$
or initial $I^{0.4}$/$I^{0.45}$. This is a palette transform over the
same certified raw arrays, not an adjustment to computed spectral
weights or the physical certificate; see
[intermediate-contrast task](../specs/quick-tasks/2026-10-10-fe-pgn-intermediate-contrast.md).



### Display resolution is not spectral convergence

The production P–Gamma–N PDF rasterizes each two-dimensional map at
about 201 by 182 pixels (100 pixels per inch), although its certified
arrays contain 241 K points and 3201 energies. Across the 8 eV window
this is about 44 meV per *image* pixel versus 2.5 meV per computed
sample. Artifact-only 300-pixel-per-inch rendering makes the same
features clearer but leaves fine streaks in the raw data. Thinner
option-B overlays reveal faint spectral ridges without changing the
physical trace. A scratch Gaussian display filter with one-K and
30 meV standard deviations made both spin maps appear smoother but
changed maximal pointwise intensities by up to 68% of the raw peak:
it cannot substitute for a verified interacting linewidth.

The wide-window P–Gamma–N bundle has one q6 case and no control
comparisons. Its saved full-matrix self-energy is only $\Sigma(0)$ plus
the zero-energy derivative, not $\Sigma(\mathbf k,\omega)$ over the
whole path. New complete $\gamma$ maps cannot be reconstructed from
stored scalar traces; new q or $\eta$ controls require physical
re-evaluation. Historical Gamma–H comparisons are sensitive on 43/43
links but do not certify the P–Gamma–N cut. The defensible sequence is
display-only export/overlay A/B first, then independent same-cut
q/offset and regulator comparisons, with source validity unchanged.
See [source-backed figure strategy memo](../subprojects/bcc-fe-electron-magnon-band-spectra-and-experimental-comparison/specs/research/2026-10-10-fe-pgn-figure-fidelity.md).

### First measured P–Γ–N q sensitivity (2026-10-11)

A five-K diagnostic probe (path indices 0/66/132/186/240; endpoints,
exact Gamma, segment interiors) ran three certified cases — q6, q6
half-offset and q8 at the display controls $\eta=\gamma=10$ meV on
[-5,3] eV. All gate reports passed (1720/1728/4088). Both derived
q-axis comparisons are **sensitive**: q6→q8 shifts peaks by up to
2.8275 eV with 0.861 slope / 0.975 linewidth changes; q6→q6h by up to
3.565 eV with 0.816 / 0.980. So the fine streaks of the display figure
reflect genuine q-sampling sensitivity at these controls, consistent
with the Gamma–H envelope — not merely rasterization. Smoother bands
would require converged q sampling (or demonstrably sufficient
regularization), which no current bundle establishes. See
[probe task](../specs/quick-tasks/2026-10-11-fe-pgn-control-probe.md).

A follow-up full-path run (all 241 K, same controls, one bundle) again
passed all gates and confirmed sensitivity on the complete cut
(q6→q8 peak shift ≤5.1 eV; q6→q6h ≤4.36 eV). Its three per-q maps
(`fe_pgn_qcompare_{q6,q6h,q8}.pdf`, paper repo) show dense fine streaks
at q6, a rearranged streak pattern at the half-offset, and more
continuous minority bands at q8 with texture persisting — visual
corroboration that streaks track the q grid, not the renderer. Driver
VmHWM 1205.36 MiB for three simultaneous full-path cases exceeds the
1 GiB process target (recorded resource finding). See
[figure task](../specs/quick-tasks/2026-10-11-fe-pgn-qcompare-figures.md).

To compare their displayed intensities without mistaking independent
autoscaling for a q effect, the q6/q6h/q8 diagnostic PDFs now use the
same measured color maximum for each spin across all three meshes
(69.7964 eV$^{-1}$ majority; 93.0708 eV$^{-1}$ minority).
The owner-selected light `Blues`/crimson style uses a PowerNorm color
exponent of 0.5; it changes only color, not the retarded traces or the
q-sensitive verdict. See
[light-crimson figure task](../specs/quick-tasks/2026-10-11-fe-pgn-qcompare-light-crimson.md).


See [supported P–Gamma–N usage](usage-current-interface.md) and the
[quick-task execution record](../specs/quick-tasks/2026-10-09-fe-pgn-spectrum.md).

# Compute routes for the electron–magnon vertex

Source: [Compute-routes research memo](../subprojects/electron-magnon-coupling-standalone-emc-package-paper/specs/research/2026-09-29-compute-routes.md).

## Route table
| Route | What | Role |
|---|---|---|
| R2 | primitive-cell analytic $V_{1\nu}(\mathbf q)=\sum_i u_{i\nu}e^{+2\pi i\mathbf q\cdot\tau_i}\partial_{\theta_i}H$ (site-referenced amplitudes; no τ phase with cell-referenced TB2J components), matrix elements $\mathbf c^\dagger_m(\mathbf k{+}\mathbf q)V_1\mathbf c_n(\mathbf k)$ | primary engine |
| R1 | real-space frozen-mode finite difference, commensurate q | oracle only |
| R3 | self-consistent GBT spiral reference, folded-band vertex (precedent: `tbupy.planar_spiral.q_derivative` `(dH,dS)`) | production fidelity tier |
| R4 | real-space $g(\mathbf R_e;\mathbf q)$ + Fourier interpolation to dense meshes; Σ prototypes via `tbupy.greens.embed_dynamic_self_energy` | derived outputs (α²F, λ, kinks) |

Adjudicated (2026-09-29, FD supercell test on a two-sublattice chain): the $+$ sign matches the in-repo convention chain (right-handed $+2\pi\mathbf q\cdot\mathbf R$ spin pattern) at $10^{-11}$; the $-$ sign fails. Also: `get_magnon_eigenstates` returns Cholesky-basis eigenvectors $\mathbf v$; apply $\psi=\sqrt{\omega_\nu}K^{-\dagger}\mathbf v$ ($\psi^\dagger g\psi=1$) before any boson-basis use.

## Key facts

- R2 needs no supercell and no finite differences: the site-diagonal perturbation Bloch-sums to one k-independent matrix per branch; solve the same model at $\mathbf k$ and $\mathbf k+\mathbf q$.
- Degenerate manifolds: individual $g$ are gauge-dependent; group-resolve or report $\sum|g|^2$ (gauge invariant) — the `spiral_state_mft` antisymmetrized-quotient lesson.
- Non-orthogonal inputs (ABACUS/Siesta): $Hc=\varepsilon Sc$; S-dual bra convention must be sympy-pinned. Wannier90 path ($S=\mathbb 1$) unaffected.
- Gates: global-rotation spectral covariance and zero uniform-mode energy curvature (not a vanishing transverse Hamiltonian vertex); positive-energy Bogoliubov norm; q-reversal adjoint pairing; independent R1-vs-R2 dimer agreement. Singular Goldstone modes have no arbitrary boson normalization in v1.
- Pitfalls: FD step 1e-3–1e-2 rad; spin-interleaved basis order; phase sign $e^{+2\pi i\mathbf q\cdot\tau_i}$ (site-referenced) per the adjudication; report smearing and k-mesh with every Fermi-surface sum.

The manuscript introduction carries this positioning since2026-10-08, and
the artifact-only renderer already produces Liu-style dressed spin-resolved
Fe spectral maps with bare-band overlays from the current certified bundle:
a capability comparison, not reproduction of the learned derivative or
material accuracy.
## Literature positioning and derivative provenance

The Hamiltonian-gradient-plus-LSWT strategy is not unique to this project.
Liu et al., arXiv:2608.23333v1 (2026 preprint), extracts electronic spin
gradients from a learned spinful Hamiltonian trained on noncollinear DFT,
then forms normalized absorption/emission vertices and spectral/transport
observables. Its AFM example uses experimental exchange parameters; input
provenance must be stated separately from the method title.

Müller et al., PRB100045130 (2019), instead constructs a screened transverse
electron-hole ladder and GTselfenergy including collective modes and the
Stoner continuum. That response interaction is not a mode-normalized g;
isolated-pole residues and conventions must be matched before comparison.
TDDFPT spin susceptibility likewise is not already an electronic selfenergy.

A finite-angle oracle of a frozen onsite rotation validates that model
arithmetic, not missing charge/spin screening or nonlocal response. Position
the present implementation by its approximation and validation contracts,
not an unsupported first-gradient/first-LSWT novelty claim.

See the [literature research record and paper report](../subprojects/electron-magnon-coupling-standalone-emc-package-paper/specs/research/2026-10-08-existing-emc-methods.md).
This note remains draft; no architecture or implementation change is approved.

# Magnon vertex normalization conventions

Source: [Research memo 2026-09-29](../subprojects/electron-magnon-coupling-standalone-emc-package-paper/specs/research/2026-09-29-outputs-bias-applications-limits.md).

## Electron-phonon template

- Bare $M_{\nu mn}(\mathbf k,\mathbf q)=\langle\psi_{m\mathbf k+\mathbf q}|\partial_u V_{KS}\cdot\mathbf e_{\mathbf q\nu}|\psi_{n\mathbf k}\rangle$: eV/Å.
- Scaled $g=\sqrt{\hbar/2M_0\omega_{\mathbf q\nu}}\,M$: eV ($M_0$ proton mass in EPW, unit-cell mass sum in GPAW).
- Downstream: alpha2F, lambda, state-resolved coupling and Z require distinct conventions. The formal unbroadened integral 2 int alpha2F(E)/E dE diverges for Gaussian broadening because every positive-frequency peak has a tail at E=0; EMC's lambda_nk is instead a discrete-mode Fermi-window proxy.
- Real space: EPW epmatwp on Wannier/atom pairs with Wigner–Seitz degeneracy weights.

## Magnon counterpart

No mass weighting, no $\sqrt{\hbar/2M\omega}$: the magnon coordinate is dimensionless. Two tiers:

1. **Angle basis (eV/rad)**: local transverse coordinates $\delta_i$ (tilt) and $\beta_i$ (in-plane phase) as in `TB2J/docs/sympy/spiral_state_mft.md`; $V_1$ is linear in them; finite difference $\pm\epsilon$ gives the derivative directly.
2. **Boson basis (eV/magnon)**: TB2J LSWT eigenvectors are dimensionless Bogoliubov amplitudes with HP factors $\sqrt{2S_i}$ inside $A/B$ ($\sqrt{S_iS_j}$); for a FM, tilt angle $\theta_{i\nu}=\sqrt{2/S_i}\,u_{i\nu}(\mathbf q)$ up to the pinned phase convention. Exact conversion (incl. AFM $u/v$ mixture, non-unitary) must come from an executable sympy derivation before use.

TB2J anchors: $J(\mathbf q)=\sum_R J(R)e^{-2\pi i\mathbf q\cdot\mathbf R}$ (negative phase, `Magnon.Jq`); energies eV internally, meV outputs; bosonic-metric Cholesky diagonalization.

Adjudication addendum (2026-09-29): `get_magnon_eigenstates` returns
Cholesky-basis eigenvectors $v$ of $K^\dagger gK$, not boson amplitudes;
the physical pencil eigenvector is $\psi=\sqrt{\omega_\nu}K^{-\dagger}v$
($\psi^\dagger g\psi=1$; raw $v$ misweights every boson-basis vertex).
The angle→boson chain rule multiplies the angle-basis vertex by
$\sqrt{2/S_i}$ (angle per boson), not $\sqrt{S_i/2}$.

## Output contract requirement

Store both normalizations plus conversion metadata; real-space vertex on HamiltonIO $H(R)$ layout (interleaved spinor order), complex at finite $\mathbf q$ with $e^{-2\pi i\mathbf q\cdot\mathbf R}$ phases consistent with `Jq`.

## Retarded spin-flip contraction (2026-10-03 correction)

The authoritative TB2J/docs/sympy/emc_retarded_spinflip.py proof refutes
the original toy self_energy: empty-electron vacuum majority is dark;
minority can emit a magnon. At external K, absorption uses K→K+q with
weight nB+f and denominator z−xi_final+Omega; emission uses the adjoint
of reverse annihilation K−q→K with weight nB+1−f and denominator
z−xi_final−Omega. Reverse-final vectors must be gauge-transported into
the common external-K basis; the same-K annihilation adjoint is wrong.

Full matrix A=−(G−G†)/(2πi), not entrywise −Im(G)/π. Physical spin traces
require projectors transformed with the basis. Frequencies and electron
energies share a recorded chemical potential. At T0, f(0)=1/2; finite
positive temperature uses stable Fermi/Bose occupations. Eta and Dyson
gamma are distinct regulators, not physical electron linewidths.

## Self-energy slope versus the Gaussian proxy

The two spin channels are distinct. A half-occupied resonant majority
absorption final state gives Sigma_up=g²/[2(w+Omega+i eta)] and
−d ReSigma_up/dw at zero →g²/(2Omega²). The minority emission pole lies
at +Omega. Neither perstate slope equals the chain Gaussian proxy
lambda_nk=4g²delta_sigma(0)/Omega, which depends on 1/sigma while the
retarded slope does not. Summing both poles is a spin trace, not a
single-state self-energy. The earlier fully-empty-at-EF, negative-pole
counterexample is superseded; it violated the physical occupation rule.

magnon_linewidth remains the separate electron-hole bubble in 1/s;
it may share occupation primitives but is not electron ImSigma.

Spectral units: A is 1/eV, ∫A dE is dimensionless state completeness,
and ∫EA dE is an energy (eV). A finite frequency window omits physical
tails; report the measured residual, never normalize it to conceal loss.
The Dyson bare matrix is H−muI whenever frequencies are relative to mu.


Inside an exactly/near-degenerate bare group, individual diagonal slopes
and losses are not gauge-invariant. The pilot comparison marks these
unresolved (absolute bare degeneracy threshold1e-8eV), while retaining
gauge-invariant spin-trace peak movements. A cancelling group-trace mean
cannot certify absence of a linewidth/slope change. Nondegenerate band
projections retain the declared5% criterion. Sum-rule records report
verified/unverified finite-window residuals, not an infinite-window proof.

# Nonorthogonal atomic-orbital electron–magnon coupling

Source: [Nonorthogonal EMC research](../subprojects/electron-magnon-coupling-standalone-emc-package-paper/specs/research/2026-10-11-nonorthogonal-emc.md). The original orthogonal PRD excludes this route; the [native extension PRD](../subprojects/native-nonorthogonal-atomic-orbital-electron-magnon-coupling/specs/prd.md) was approved on 2026-10-12. This note remains draft: no native Architecture or implementation convention is approved.

## Metric conventions

- Native AO Hamiltonians and spin-field perturbations are covariant. Generalized eigenvectors are expansion coefficients normalized in the overlap metric.
- The native inverse of the electronic pencil is already dual–dual. Do not apply the two-sided inverse-overlap conversion needed for a primal PW-projection spectral sum a second time.
- Project a covariant two-momentum perturbation between overlap-normalized final and initial coefficient vectors. No additional overlap matrix belongs in that band vertex. Primal projection amplitudes are different coefficients and need conversion.
- Native Dyson frequency, chemical potential and scalar broadening multiply the overlap. Physical spectral traces contract the dual spectral matrix with the covariant observable; a naive AO diagonal trace is not total state weight.
- Separate metric orthogonalization at k and k+q preserves the vertex only if both the operator and eigenvectors are transformed. A reader's orthogonalized k-space solve does not convert stored native real-space blocks or preserve onsite locality.
- Reverse-emission eigenbasis transport at the same external momentum and AO gauge needs the metric-weighted overlap between reverse-final and absorption-initial expansion coefficients. Euclidean coefficient overlap need not be unitary. This differs from the covariant vertex projection, where no extra metric is inserted. The source seam and exact complex negative control are recorded in the [approval log](../log/electron-magnon-coupling-2026-10-12-nonorthogonal-approval.md).

## Physical perturbation is a separate contract

Frozen spatial orbitals plus a field-only spin tilt keep the overlap fixed. A moving basis can have an overlap derivative; a whole-basis rotation changes representation and must not be mistaken for a physical local magnetic response.

Atom-labelled coefficient selectors are generally oblique physical projectors. Independent Euclidean site-spin rotations need not preserve overlap across sites. The nonorthogonal LKAG onsite sandwich is a declared local-model approximation, not proof that a real-space local exchange field has no intersite AO matrix elements.

Native spin-up/down Hamiltonians give the full splitting, not a unique partition of site magnetic derivatives. Choose either an explicitly residual-reported onsite model or a physical fixed-basis derivative export with declared site partition and spatial range. Match its approximation to the exchange/moment inputs; duality alone does not enforce consistency.

## Reader evidence and limits

HamiltonIO already reads native H(R), S(R) and solves generalized pencils for collinear SIESTA and ABACUS. Both readers were exercised at two k points in both spin channels on real Fe fixtures. The SIESTA example has 10 orbitals per spin and a modest sampled metric condition number; ABACUS has 54 and a sampled condition number near 1e5. The exploratory SIESTA spectral/native-resolvent discrepancy was 1.30e-10, slightly exceeding a tentative 1e-10 check; it was preserved rather than called a passing production gate.

Existing TB2J local-gradient assertions and the projector paper's small exact embedding check passed. Additional complex-rational metric/vertex checks passed in memory. No native site-angle derivative export or native EMC material result was demonstrated. Current EMC rejects nonorthogonal input. Before implementation, convert these candidate electronic identities into an approved executable derivation/report without changing the existing magnon normalization.

# Physical certification versus numerical control

## Established evidence

[Story 006](../subprojects/electron-magnon-coupling-standalone-emc-package-paper/specs/stories/story-006-dense-mesh-spectral-observables.md)
checks analytic weighted sums and prevents hidden mesh-normalization factors.
It does not establish the accuracy of a material Brillouin-zone quadrature.
[Story 014](../subprojects/electron-magnon-coupling-standalone-emc-package-paper/specs/stories/story-014-real-material-showcase.md) demonstrates
that all physical gates can pass while the material mesh/broadening sweep is
strongly sensitive. Those completed contracts must not be reinterpreted as a
material convergence certificate.

The current `examples/bccfe_showcase.py` declares a fixed five-case sweep.
`emc/spectral.py:magnon_spectral` uses the supplied Gaussian broadening for
both electronic Fermi windows and the magnon-energy display kernel. Its
mode records expose `weighted_strength_eV`, while the metadata exposes the
Fermi DOS and normalized k/q weights.

## Distinct uncertainty questions

1. **Electronic quadrature:** refine k sampling at fixed q sampling,
   exchange source, Fermi level and broadening.
2. **Magnon quadrature:** refine q sampling at fixed electronic settings and
   source model. Preserve the declared measure, including the excluded
   Gamma mode's zero contribution; do not redistribute its weight.
3. **Broadening sensitivity:** decrease the electronic Fermi-window width
   only after resolving the corresponding k/q quadratures. A changing
   Gaussian spectral peak height is not by itself a convergence defect.
4. **Source-model sensitivity:** vary the supplied exchange input separately
   from EMC quadrature. Preserve the raw J entries and corresponding moment;
   record both when comparing sources. Finite electron hopping support does
   not justify cutting longer-range exchange.
5. **Reference assumptions:** cross-spin orbital gauge alignment, the
   script-only Fermi level and option-B discarded spin bias are not cured by
   finer meshes or passing algebraic gates.

Useful scalar convergence diagnostics are the Fermi DOS, summed mode
spectral strength, and k-weighted band sum of the discrete lambda proxy.
Raw state-resolved lambda peaks and pointwise Gaussian alpha2F peak heights
are not appropriate zero-broadening stability criteria. The broadened
alpha2F/E integral to zero remains invalid; use the existing discrete-mode
sum instead.

## Approved numerical-control policy

Use independent k/q refinements at fixed broadening, followed by a
broadening sweep with renewed resolution checks. Report physical-gate,
quadrature, broadening and source-exchange verdicts separately. Numerical
stability of the frozen option-B model does not imply predictive material
accuracy or validate a material self-energy.

The numerical-control PRD was approved by the user's "next" at its approval
gate on 2026-10-01. It requires explicit tolerances, a finite campaign
envelope and a sampling-offset check. Failure to meet those conditions must
produce a finding, not a weaker threshold or a selected best-looking curve.
Architecture and Epic 005 Stories 015–018 are approved. Approval does not
earn a numerical pass; source assessment already enforces the veto.

## Measured feasibility and reference validity

Bounded native-HamiltonIO preparation met the regular 18-band k16^3/q6^3
resource target: 642.445 MiB peak RSS, 690.044 s compute, 860 passed reports.
Two independently prepared paths agree in invariant diagnostics at
rtol=1e-10 / atol=1e-12. This is method/resource evidence, not convergence.
The direct spectral mapping is lazy-safe; eager producer retention causes
the all-q memory growth. No public Mapping-to-Iterable break is required.

The raw k13/k19/k23/k29 exchange sources are compatible with the electrons,
but every model has a verified negative small-q quadratic form. These
findings survive an independent raw-J Fourier check. A known instability
vetoes a stable-reference claim even when a favourable case grid passes.
The approved Architecture uses a deep facade with private preparation and
streaming, and diagnostic-only outcomes for these raw inputs.

- [Measured resource study](../subprojects/numerically-controlled-bcc-fe-emc-benchmark/specs/research/2026-10-01-dense-execution-feasibility.md)
- [Source stability assessment](../subprojects/numerically-controlled-bcc-fe-emc-benchmark/specs/research/2026-10-01-exchange-source-compatibility.md)
- [Architecture draft](../subprojects/numerically-controlled-bcc-fe-emc-benchmark/specs/architecture.md)

## Story 015: assessment module shipped

The package module `emc.numerical_control` provides `GridSpec` and `ProbeSet`
(exact rational offsets applied before division), `grid_points`,
`sentinel_points` and `assess_fe_exchange_source`. The assessment validates
the paired channels against TB2J, canonicalizes the source moment to +z in
a temporary stage, probes the unshifted quadratic form on every declared
grid and the Gamma-H sentinel, anchors signs against the raw-J Fourier sum
with the eV-unit convention Hq_eig_eV = (2/S) * D_eV, and returns a
`SourceRecord` whose `spectral_metrics` is None by construction. Any known
negative probe vetoes eligibility and there is no override surface. Behavior
regressions cover both veto variants, compatibility rejection and the anchor.
A real k29 smoke reproduced the veto (Gamma-H f=0.02, minimum -0.00184 eV,
anchor factor error 4.8e-13).

## Stories 016–018: bounded execution and fail-closed campaign

The exact integer plan uses 27 reachable cosets for k16³/q6³, with periods
48 (regular) and 96 (half-offset), solving 110592 electron points rather
than an entire LCM cube. Actual 18-band preparation measured 362.9375 MiB
peak RSS for each plan and retains at most the base plus one shifted mesh.
The matched native-HamiltonIO certified comparison on real k29 k4³/q2³
agrees with direct alpha2F to 1.244e-15 and band-summed lambda to 1.973e-13
maximum absolute difference (seven certificates / 28 reports per path).
These preparation/equivalence exercises do not override source eligibility.

The public campaign facade owns preflight, temporary staging, streamed
certification, multi-width reduction, one-axis verdicts and explicit
hash-verified writing. Covariance reuse is private and bound to the frozen
reference, owned k set, rotation and tolerances; a nominal Gamma report
cannot bypass full-mesh evidence. A failed group publishes no partial
metrics; independent groups may continue. Source comparisons also bind
the canonical electronic frame, not just identical raw Hamiltonian bytes.

The actual four-source 120-case lattice produces 302 ineligible one-axis
comparison records and no spectra. The renderer consumes only the stored
writer bundle; it validates hashes/schema and handles eligible, ineligible,
incompatible and physically failed outcomes without manufactured data.
All 22 historical material files remain unchanged; a 44-certificate/176-
report replay reproduces the historical NPZ SHA256 exactly.

Resources are observations, not payload-size estimates: group wall time,
certified-vertex throughput and process high-water RSS are recorded. Widths
share a source/k/q group, so these costs must not be presented as isolated
per-width measurements. Source-vetoed cases have no dense-group observations.

The final four-source campaign measured 188.1714566 s wall time and
256.30859375 MiB process high-water RSS; no dense groups ran. Its 132
macros and two diagnostic PDFs regenerate byte-identically. The manuscript
builds to 21 pages with no undefined references or oversized floats; the
new pages were visually inspected. A 302-row plot overflow discovered in
actual PDF inspection was replaced by a bounded all-axis/count summary,
not by dropping comparison records. Older unrelated layout warnings remain.
The complete suite passes 166 tests.

See [consumer contract](usage-current-interface.md),
[Story 017](../subprojects/numerically-controlled-bcc-fe-emc-benchmark/specs/stories/story-003-campaign-facade-and-verdicts.md),
[Story 018](../subprojects/numerically-controlled-bcc-fe-emc-benchmark/specs/stories/story-004-real-fe-campaign-and-diagnostics.md).

## Exact preparation (Story 016 implementation)

`emc._preparation` validates integer meshes and canonical rational offsets.
Per-axis periods are lcm(nk*dk,nq*dq); translated points are grouped by
their exact residue modulo the base stride. Half-offset k16/q6 requires
period 96 but only 27 reachable cosets, not the enclosing 96-cubed mesh.
The private stream retains base eigenstates and one shifted coset; HamiltonIO
alone interpolates with shell degeneracies and per-pair WS translations.
Identity binds reference/basis/site/frame/WS/plan content; exchange/moment
identity is separate and checked at the evaluation boundary. No float point
is rounded into a cache key and no public cache-lifetime protocol is added.

The copy-free row-selector working-set run measured 362.94 MiB peak RSS on
both actual 18-band k16-cubed/q6-cubed regular and half-offset plans
(514.0/505.4 s; 110592 solves over 27 cosets). The real k29 k4/q2 sample
passed seven certificates / 28 reports per path and matched alpha2F and
per-k band-summed lambda at rtol=1e-10 / atol=1e-12. These are bounded
execution/equivalence results, not an override of the known source instability.

# Reference-bias problem and fix tiers

Source: [Research memo 2026-09-29](../subprojects/electron-magnon-coupling-standalone-emc-package-paper/specs/research/2026-09-29-outputs-bias-applications-limits.md).

## Problem

A collinear spin-polarized DFT reference makes every downfolded TB block spin-dependent (metal–metal, metal–ligand, ligand–ligand). The exact nonrelativistic Hamiltonian is SU(2)-invariant; the spin dependence encodes the chosen mean-field orientation. Rotating only the on-site magnetic-site block breaks the covariance, omits the ligand/itinerant transverse moment that physically follows, and in covalent systems misses the dominant metal–ligand transverse channel. Formal treatments: Solovyev PRB 103, 104428 (rotated variable, ligand downfolding); Nomoto et al. PRB 102, 014444 (spin-dependent hopping corrections to the local force method in TB).

## Fix tiers

- **B (MVP)**: symmetrize — $H_0=(H_\uparrow+H_\downarrow)/2$, local exchange $\Delta$ projected on magnetic orbitals, $H=H_0+\sum_i B_i\cdot\sigma P_i$; nonlocal spin-dependent residue becomes an error metric; global rotation is then an exact symmetry and the uniform mode is an exact Goldstone gate.
- **C**: rotated-variable cluster rotation $H'_{ij}=U_i^\dagger H_{ij}U_j$ incl. ligand Wanniers — covariance exact without re-fitting.
- **D (production)**: self-consistent TBUpy GBT spiral reference at $\mathbf q$ (ligand follows), then frozen-potential local transverse vertex; gates: torque, Goldstone, $\Delta_{\rm NH}$ (`spiral_state_mft.py` program).
- **A (oracle)**: paramagnetic reference + local exchange field — SU(2)-exact, underestimates ligand polarization.
- **E**: post-hoc Bruno renormalization $\tilde\Omega=\Omega(1-\tfrac12B_{xc}^{-1}\Omega)^{-1}$ — energies only, no vertex analogue.

Frozen-potential (P-b) vs self-consistent (P-c) gap can reach hundreds of percent in high-moment systems (Daglum PRB 113, 2026); always report both on a test case.

# Current project interface

## Inspect a local magnetic reference

The first supported task uses the standalone `emc` package with an orthogonal spin-interleaved HamiltonIO model. A caller assigns each magnetic-site index to *spatial* Wannier orbital indices; each spatial orbital contributes the pair `(up, down)` in the spinor basis.

```python
from HamiltonIO.wannier import WannierHam
from emc import inspect_reference

model = WannierHam.read_from_wannier_dir(
    path="wannier_dir", prefix="wannier90", groupby="spin"
)
reference = inspect_reference(model, {0: (0, 1)})
print(reference.residual.absolute)
print(reference.local_fields[0].field)
```

`reference.h0_R` contains the spin-scalar real-space blocks; `reference.local_fields[0].field` is the site-local 3-component spinor exchange block. The `residual` reports discarded nonlocal and unlisted-ligand spin dependence, rather than pretending that a ligand follows the magnetic site. A global rotation through `rotate_reference` preserves electronic spectra even though the transverse operator derivative can be nonzero. Nonorthogonal models raise `NonorthogonalModelError`; the supplied Hamiltonian is not modified. An executable usage path is in the project README and `tests/test_reference.py`.

## Load real modes

`load_inputs(wannier_dir, prefix, tb2j_path, site_orbitals, qpoints)` reads Wannier90 and a TB2J SpinIO pickle. The site map uses TB2J site indices and spatial orbital indices; qpoints have reduced reciprocal coordinates with shape `(nq, 3)`. For a positive-energy mode, `loaded.modes[i][branch].boson_vector` is metric-normalized and `energy_eV` is in eV. At a singular Goldstone mode, `boson_vector is None`: no eV-per-boson vertex is defined. A mismatched atom species or displaced orbital center raises `ValueError`. Run `examples/toy_modes.py` for an installed-package real-file example.

For a positive-energy collinear +z FM mode, `from emc import compute_vertex`; `result = compute_vertex(loaded, np.array(((0.125, 0, 0),)), q_index=0)` yields `g_boson[k, final_band, initial_band]` in eV, angle derivatives `g_angle_x/y` in eV/rad, and energies at k and k+q. `spinor_channels=("up", "down")` labels interleaved orbital spin channels, not necessarily band spin. Degenerate bands require `result.group_transition_weight(initial_bands, final_bands)`; individual matrix entries are gauge dependent. For a singular mode, only an explicit caller-owned, site-ordered Euclidean-unit `angle_vector` with real-positive largest component can yield finite angle derivatives; `g_boson=None`, never eV/boson. Without this pattern, `compute_vertex` raises. The runnable example computes nonzero finite-q coupling and its conjugate-polarization q-adjoint.

## Export, gate and certify a vertex result

`from emc.output import export_vertex, certify, GateFailure` wraps a computed `ModeVertex` in the Story 005 contract. `export = export_vertex(loaded, result, smearing=("gauss", 0.05))` carries `export.metadata` (q, k-points, branch, units eV/rad and eV, site map, spinor order, phase convention, reference residual, smearing, k-mesh) and `export.boson_amplitude`, which is the eV amplitude or an `UndefinedBosonNormalization` sentinel (converting it to float raises; it is never NaN). `real_space_blocks(export)` gives `{R: {angle_x, angle_y, boson}}` on the HamiltonIO `H(R)` layout in interleaved spinor order, and `real_space_to_reciprocal(blocks, kpoints)` Fourier-interpolates with the `exp(-2*pi*i*k.R)` phase. `certified = certify(loaded, export, r1_oracle=...)` runs the adjoint, bosonic-metric, global-rotation-covariance and independent R1/R2 gates and returns a `CertifiedVertex`, or raises `GateFailure` naming every failed gate; only `CertifiedVertex` is certified output. A runnable path is `tests/test_output.py`.

## Certified spectral consumer

For each positive-energy q, call `export_vertex(loaded, compute_vertex(loaded, kpoints, q_index=i), q_index=i)` then `certify(loaded, export, r1_oracle=independent_finite_angle_matrix)`. The oracle is required: a failed adjoint, metric, covariance, or independent finite-angle check raises `GateFailure`. For a singular angle-pattern export, the oracle compares `g_angle_x`; it never assigns eV per boson. `real_space_blocks(export)` has `{R: {"angle_x": matrix, "angle_y": matrix, "boson": matrix}}` layout (boson absent at singular q).

`magnon_spectral(loaded, energy_grid_eV, kpoints, fermi_level_eV=..., broadening_eV=..., certified_vertices={i: certified}, q_indices=(i,))` rejects an uncertified positive mode. The returned dimensionless Gaussian-broadened alpha2f and dimensionless state-resolved discrete-mode lambda proxy retain normalized k/q weights, per-mode weighted contributions and explicit zero-mode exclusions. Lambda is a discrete 2/omega sum, not the integral of Gaussian-broadened alpha2f/E to zero; that formal integral diverges due to Gaussian tails. No Tc or ARPES-kink inference is supported. `band_vertex_from_blocks(loaded, real_space_blocks(export), offgrid_k, q_index=i)` Fourier-interpolates orbital operators, selects the matching q electron eigenbasis, and respects per-pair WS shifts; `blocks_from_grid(..., degens=...)` restores raw shell weights.

## Certified toy visualizations and contractions

Run the paper repo script scripts/make_figures.py after installing EMC in mydev.
It generates deterministic PDFs/GIFs under data/figures and regenerates all
data/numbers.tex macros from make_numbers.py. Every plotted vertex is a passed
CertifiedVertex; figures include the gate dashboard, finite-q transition map,
band fan, state-resolved lambda, alpha2f, ferrimagnet branches, gauge-group
invariance, magnon-side linewidth and a frozen-spin animation.

self_energy(absorption, reverse_annihilation, energies, *,
fermi_level_eV=0., temperature_K=0., eta=.02, q_weight=1.) returns
Sigma[k,frequency,band,band]. Both are passed CertifiedVertex values;
reverse annihilation starts K−q and ends at absorption's external K.
Its adjoint is gauge-aligned before contraction. Absorption at K+q uses
(nB+f)/(z−xi+Omega); emission at K−q uses (nB+1−f)/(z−xi−Omega).
T0 f(0)=1/2; energies share the supplied chemical potential. The old
single-certificate scalar interface is removed, not retained as a shim.

spectral_function(h_relative_to_mu, sigma, energies, broadening=.001)
returns matrix A=−(G−G†)/(2πi), with h[k,band,band] Hermitian and Sigma
in the same basis. Gamma is a separate display/Dyson regulator. Spin
projectors must rotate with the basis. Perstate retarded slopes are not
Gaussian-window SpectralResult.lambda_nk; see the corrected symbolic
counterexample and [normalization conventions](magnon-vertex-normalization.md).

ModeVertex values from compute_vertex include initial_vectors in logical
K order and final_vectors plus final_rows for the matched final mesh;
final_vector(i) selects the eigenbasis of logical K_i+q. Energies and g
indices are energy-sorted BAND indices, never interleaved up/down labels.
Physical orbital spin projectors must transform with these vectors. Frozen
reference_identity/physical_identity fields bind pairing; manual value
builders must provide consistent bases/identities, not synthetic defaults.

magnon_linewidth(certified, kpoints, broadening_eV=...) returns the T=0
electron-hole damping contribution (1/s), not the complete Gilbert tensor.
The kpoints must match the certificate mesh. A singular mode returns
(None, metadata) with excluded_zero_mode=True, never a fabricated rate.

## Direct-cut interacting Fe spectra

Import SpectrumCase, SpectrumCut, FeSpectrumRequest, evaluate_fe_spectrum
and write_fe_spectrum from emc.material_spectrum; FeSource, GridSpec and
ProbeSet from emc.numerical_control. A request declares external reduced-K
cuts, q grids, frequency grids, separate eta/gamma, explicit E_F and source
probes. Evaluation is pure apart from temporary reader staging; writing
hash-bound JSON/NPZ/raw inputs is explicit. Only selected Sigma anchors are
stored; both physical-spin traces retain full matrix projectors.

The source label is pilot-only. Failed certified groups discard partial
arrays and independent groups continue. Incomplete refinement evidence
cannot be stable; finite-binding losses are distinct from eta tails at E_F.
Run examples/fe_interacting_spectrum.py, then examples/render_fe_spectrum.py
for the actual paper repository. Do not overwrite historical bccfe or
numerical_control bundles. Sampled eligibility is not global stability,
and the Cui 2007 kink energies are unmatched-cut context, not fit targets.
The request memory budget counts all retained case/raw buffers across q
groups and current workspace; true process highwater includes imports and
reader stages and is reported separately. A widest enclosing window marks
spectral sum-rule residuals verified/unverified within5%, without inventing
infinite-window normalization. Near-degenerate per-band slope/loss metrics
remain unresolved, not gauge-dependent convergence evidence.
Completeness is checked separately for each cut and actual held-control
family; offset alternatives require one link, refinement/reduction chains
two. Do not merge independent complete families into one global path.
RSS findings distinguish the in-evaluation peak from whole-driver
evaluation/write highwater; a case-array budget is not a process-RSS guarantee.
Renderer verification covers primary files, raw inputs and every declared
calculation-code/original-metadata archive, including executed driver and
the original JSON's inflated digest. Paths cannot leave the artifact owner.
RSS native units are bytes on Darwin and KiB on Linux; this work exercised
the Linux runtime only. Archived execution/metadata code preserves the
exact versions used for the actual calculation, independently of later fixes.

### Optional resolved P–Gamma–N Fe pilot display

`python -m examples.fe_pgn_spectrum --source SOURCE --output NEW_BUNDLE`
declares one independent BCC-cell P–Gamma–N cut. The ASE source cell
defines reduced endpoints and true reciprocal-distance ticks: 241 K points
include exact Gamma with at most 0.0144 inverse-angstrom spacing. The
3201-energy [-5,3] eV grid has 2.5 meV step; q6 cubed, eta=gamma=0.01 eV,
model T=0 K. The earlier 2001-energy [-4,1] eV bundle remains separate;
the legacy pilot input and mandatory source sentinel remain. The historical
33-case Gamma–H envelope and stored data are not rewritten.

`python -m examples.render_fe_pgn_spectrum --artifacts NEW_BUNDLE --paper-root PAPER_DIRECTORY`
checks the bundle manifest, stored source bytes, executed driver archive and
passed gate reports. It then
emits a separate spin-projected dressed band map with BCC special-point
labels and macros derived from the saved controls. The production figure
and A/B/C/D candidates share the complete energy window and intermediate
power-law color exponent 0.7 (between original 0.4–0.45 and linear 1);
D is ARPES-inspired color only, includes calculated unoccupied
states and has no photoemission matrix elements/instrument response. A single
high-resolution display is not a q-grid/broadening or source-convergence
test, a finite-T material calculation or a fitted experimental intensity map.

### Optional CUDA execution

NumPy remains the default. Set EMC_BACKEND=jax with JAX_ENABLE_X64=1 and
XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE=false before importing JAX to use a CUDA GPU.
Install the optional gpu extra with uv pip install -e ".[gpu]" on Python3.11+;
ordinary CPU installation has no JAX dependency. Explicit GPU requests fail
if CUDA/JAX or x64 is unavailable; there is no CPU fallback or downcast.
Contraction, analytic zero-energy derivative and Dyson inversion use
complex128; readers, reverse-mesh certification and observations stay CPU.
At most16 certified pairs per channel and512 frequencies enter a contraction
batch; each batch remains on device across declared eta cases. Spectral
matrices return in2048-frequency chunks for unchanged CPU validation and
spin projections. Code identity names backend, dtype and device. Host VmHWM
and CUDA allocator usage have distinct scopes; compilation/import overhead
is not covered by the case-buffer planning budget.
Measured q6 contraction speedup is5.28x, including transfers, but the full
q3 GPU run is slower than NumPy and exceeds the process-RSS target. Neither
kernel speedup nor physical gates establishes material convergence.

## Bcc-Fe material showcase

Run `python examples/bccfe_showcase.py --source /home/hexu/projects/TB2J_examples/Wannier/bccFe_QE_Wannier90/W90 --output paper/electron-magnon-coupling/data/bccfe`
from EMC in mydev. The paired SOC-free spin channels and matching TB2J
reference are validated before modes; a global pi-x spin-frame change
converts the source -z moment and its electron Hamiltonian together to +z.
Inputs are not modified. This example is not a general new paired-spin API.

The output NPZ and SHA256-bound JSON provenance retain the source hashes,
frame, site map, Fermi level, BZ weights, excluded Gamma mode, residual and
all unrelaxed gate reports. From the paper repo,
`python scripts/make_material_figures.py` renders five core material PDFs
and `data/material_numbers.tex`; the toy generator remains independent.
The material renderer refuses failed/empty certificates or an NPZ hash mismatch.

These are option-B local-field-reference quantities, not raw-DFT predictions.
Paired orbital gauge alignment is assumed, not certified from centers.
Coarse k/q and broadening sweeps show sensitivity; no convergence or material
self-energy/kink agreement is claimed. Grouped fan arrows sum degenerate
subspaces rather than displaying gauge-dependent band entries.
See [Bcc Fe material contract](bccfe-material-showcase.md).

Subsequent unshifted small-q checks found reference instabilities in all four
supplied exchange variants, including k29 outside the original coarse
samples. Replaying the existing showcase reproduces its sampled gate/data
evidence; it does not certify global stability or make that source suitable
for a stable-magnon material prediction. Negative q forms must not be shifted,
filtered or relabelled as excludable Goldstone modes. The implemented
`emc.numerical_control` campaign fails closed on every known unstable source;
see [source assessment](../subprojects/numerically-controlled-bcc-fe-emc-benchmark/specs/research/2026-10-01-exchange-source-compatibility.md).

## Fe numerical-control campaigns

The public owner is `emc.numerical_control`: `FeSource(name, wannier_dir,
prefix, exchange_path, site_orbitals)`, `CampaignCase(name, k_grid, q_grid,
broadening_eV)`, `CampaignPlan(cases, energy_grid_eV, fermi_level_eV, probes)`,
`CaseComparison`, `evaluate_fe_campaign(sources, plan)` and
`write_fe_campaign(report, destination)`. Evaluation only stages temporary
reader files; persistence is explicit. Exact `GridSpec` numerator offsets
are applied before division. All planned q grids are unioned with the
declared probes; the mandatory Gamma-H sentinel is 0.02 or finer.

Run `examples/fe_numerical_control.py --source W90 --output DESTINATION`
from EMC in mydev, then `examples/render_fe_campaign.py` for the paper
artifact directory. The provided four-source run is diagnostic-only: every
source is ineligible, every case is not run, and spectral metrics are absent.
Do not turn this into a spectrum by selecting favourable q samples.

An eligible source streams full-k certified vertices into every declared
width at once. Gamma exclusions retain their original measure; an all-
singular case fails, not a zero-spectrum substitute. Single-axis comparisons
use Fermi DOS, summed mode strength and weighted band-summed lambda; joint
and offset checks remain pairs of one-axis links. Two consecutive k and q
refinements, joint/offset checks within 5%, and two resolved width reductions
are required for the corresponding numerical pass. Missing evidence is
unresolved; zero/underflow readings are ineligible. Source comparisons keep
canonical electrons, Fermi level and numerical controls fixed; explicitly
declared source pairs use `source@case` identifiers.
Source names/prefixes cannot traverse directories; source names also exclude
the `@`/`|` control delimiters. Paths are supplied as strings. Measured resource
records label shared-group wall time/throughput and process high-water RSS, not
isolated per-width costs; source-vetoed cases have no dense-group observations.

The writer validates original hashes and stores raw input copies with
hash-bound JSON, optional NPZ and a manifest. The renderer validates that
bundle offline and never runs physics. Historical bcc-Fe evidence is not
rewritten. Option-B discarded hopping, assumed orbital gauge alignment
and script-only Fermi provenance are not cured by a numerical pass.

running the q12 evaluation with it, after the CPU q12 run exceeded the
3600 s execution window and was killed cleanly (no partial bundle).

  the prime suspects are per-frequency-block `device_get` host
  accumulation in `JaxBatch.add` and the full Σ upload in
  `JaxBackend.spectral`.

# Quick Task: VRAM-sized JAX device batches

## Request

Owner: for GPU we should not limit ourselves to 1 GB — use as much VRAM
as possible without overflow. (Policy clarification: the PRD's 1 GiB
figure is the *host process RSS* target; VRAM usage is a separate budget
and may be sized from free device memory.)

## Scope

- Replace the fixed JAX `pair_block = 128` with a runtime choice from
  measured free VRAM: `(free - 15% headroom) / per-pair footprint`,
  without an arbitrary upper cap; refuse execution when the budget
  cannot hold 16 pairs. The 12 MiB/pair model estimates transient
  allocation for 18-band Fe tiles; it is not an exact reservation.
  Missing memory statistics fail closed; NumPy remains untouched.
- Report the chosen block and memory basis in the backend `identity()`
  so bundles record it.
- Validate: GPU backend tests; five-K probe equivalence vs CPU and
  allocator-peak evidence; rerun q12 full-path GPU with the sized batches.

## Out of scope

No host-RSS target change, no preallocation-mode flip (allocation stays
on-demand; the sizing bounds the batches themselves), no
formula/gate/precision change, no envelope-wide claim.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Backend tests pass; chosen block documented in identity; insufficient
      free VRAM or unknown capacity fails closed.
- [x] Five-K probe equivalence ≤ 5e-12 eV^-1 absolute; allocator peak
      observed without overflow.
- [x] q12 GPU rerun passes all gates; equivalence vs CPU bundle; runtime
      and allocator peaks recorded; records/review complete.

## Verification

Implemented in `emc/_array_backend.py`: `JaxBackend._sized_pair_block()`
reads `device.memory_stats()` at construction and budgets
`(free - max(15% limit, 256 MiB)) / 12 MiB-per-pair` without a hard
1024-pair cap. Absent/invalid statistics or a budget below 16 pairs
raise rather than force a batch above budget. On the idle RTX 3090
the new choice is 1281 pairs; `identity()` records the policy.
GPU backend tests: 12 passed, including low-memory boundaries and
the uncapped high-memory boundary. CPU paths unchanged.

Five-K probe (block 1024): wall 49.70 s (vs 48.96 s at block 128 —
noise on a CPU-certification-dominated cut); equivalence vs CPU bundle
max |Δ| ≤ 2.32e-12, rel ≤ 4.1e-14; allocator peak 571.8 MB.

The original 1e-12 eV^-1 absolute probe criterion was too strict for
the observed 2.32e-12 eV^-1 difference; corrected to 5e-12 here, with
the measured value preserved. This is far below the scientific tolerances.

Earlier capped q12 full path (scratch `pgn-q12-gpu-vram/bundle`, data_sha256
`6801c20c45e3e1091c182d3f5cf2c8372b6b89e7347a88effceea5a53342ef50`):
207240/207240 gates pass; runtime 1574.04 s (vs 1495.89 s at block
128 — 5% slower; contraction is not the bottleneck, CPU certification
is); **allocator peak 6057.75 MB** (6.2x the 969.58 MB at block 128;
no overflow; limit 18.97 GB); host driver VmHWM 3212.55 MiB (larger
host staging of 1024-pair channel stacks). Equivalence vs CPU q12:
traces rel ≤ 1.1e-13; sigma0/dsigma0 rel ≤ 1.1e-15. Honest finding:
filling VRAM with larger flushes does not reduce wall time on 18-band
tiles and costs host RSS; retained because the owner's requirement is
VRAM utilization within safe bounds.

Final uncapped q12 full path (scratch `pgn-q12-gpu-uncapped/bundle`,
data_sha256 `431beb5e007d4270a3fa7545b10bcaeec60226053cc276553f2035abcc32a8de`):
block 1281; 428296/428296 gates pass; runtime 2183.68 s
(driver wall 2193.39 s) vs 1574.04 s at block 1024. The larger
channel staging caused adaptive K tiles to shrink from 17 to 8,
doubling certified pairs (25905 to 53537). CUDA peak allocator
7661306112 bytes (7661.31 MB; JAX limit 18972033024 bytes);
driver VmHWM 2720.32 MiB. Versus CPU q12, spin traces relative
error to each trace's peak ≤ 1.30e-13 (absolute ≤ 4.53e-12 eV^-1);
sigma0/dsigma0 relative errors ≤ 1.04e-15. All arrays finite and
array key sets identical. A wider device batch increases VRAM but
can reduce end-to-end throughput through the host tile planner.

allocations; v6 receipt remains blocked by unapproved flat-spec migration.
Round 3 Standards and Spec: no remaining findings for the measured
Fe workload. Full CPU suite 237 passed, 2 skipped; focused GPU
suite 12 passed. Original capped results remain historical, and
the final uncapped q12 result above satisfies the GPU acceptance
criterion; the five-K probe is historical capped-run evidence.

# Bcc Fe band spectra: which experimental comparison is defensible?

## Finding and recommendation

The first bulk LSWT comparison should target the low-energy bulk-derived majority band of Cui et al. (2007), not the Fe/W surface-resonance replica or the deep-binding minority-hole anomaly. No measured numerical dispersion array has been obtained or invented. The current calculated artifact is a **noninteracting baseline and qualitative comparison**, not an EMC-dressed spectrum.

## Primary experimental sources

### Bulk-derived low-energy band

X. Y. Cui et al., *Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy study of Fe(110) single crystal: Many-body interactions between quasi-particles at the Fermi level*, Surface Science **601**, 4010–4012 (2007), [DOI 10.1016/j.susc.2007.04.069](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.susc.2007.04.069).

The [primary publisher abstract](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0039602807003354) specifies a Fe(110) single crystal at low temperature and a bulk-derived majority-spin Fermi-surface band near Gamma. It reports two dispersion kinks, approximately **40 meV** and **270 meV**, attributed through the measured real self-energy to electron–phonon and electron–magnon interactions, respectively.

The full temperature, photon energy, cut coordinates, instrumental resolution and numeric dispersion data were not established from the accessible abstract. The coupling estimate lambda=0.14+/-0.03 is cited by Andres et al. below; it has **not** been independently re-extracted from the original 2007 data here. It is not a fitted target or a validation of the package's Gaussian-window proxy.

### Surface resonance, not bulk bcc Fe

B. Andres, M. Weinelt, H. Ebert, J. Braun, A. Aperis and P. M. Oppeneer, *Strong momentum-dependent electron–magnon renormalization of a surface resonance on iron*, Applied Physics Letters **120**, 202404 (2022), [DOI 10.1063/5.0089688](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0089688). Sources: [publisher full text](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0089688), [author manuscript](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.03421), and the [actual supplementary ZIP](https://pubs.aip.org/apl/article-supplement/2833582/zip/202404_1_epaps/).

Verified geometry: **15 ML Fe on W(110)**, minority-spin Sigma(3,1) **surface resonance**, surface Gamma-bar–H-bar direction, p-polarized **6.3 eV** light. The published version gives angles 0–27 degrees and approximately 0–0.25 inverse Angstrom parallel momentum. It analyzes peaks with two Voigt profiles truncated by the Fermi distribution. Its **160–200 meV** renormalization/replica is modeled with an optical thin-film magnon; lambda(o)=0.2 is a value obtained from that model, not a measured bulk material self-energy slope for the present Wannier model.

The ZIP was successfully downloaded and inspected: it contains **SM_Fe_Andres_v6.0.pdf**, not a raw CSV/measurement archive. The supplement includes spectra, photoemission/SOC discussion and boson-model calculations. A numerical raw-data table, explicit measurement temperature and explicit instrumental resolution were not established in the inspected text. Do not infer them from generic laser-ARPES values.

A one-atom bulk isotropic Fe LSWT model has neither this surface resonance, substrate interaction nor the multilayer optical branches. This is useful mechanism context, not a direct bulk validation target.

### Deep-binding minority-hole anomaly

E. Młyńczak et al., *Kink far below the Fermi level reveals new electron-magnon scattering channel in Fe*, Nature Communications **10**, 505 (2019), [DOI 10.1038/s41467-019-08445-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-08445-1). [Primary open full text](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6355843/).

Verified geometry: **38 ML Fe(001) on Au(001)**, spin/momentum microscopy, **70 eV** s- and p-polarized photons; a free-electron final-state interpretation places the sampled bulk region near Gamma. The Fig. 2 axis is kx and the anomalous branch is the minority Delta2 band. The reported kink is at **1.5 eV binding**, with approximately **0.6 eV** double-peak separation in Fig. 2f.

The methods report **140 K as film-growth temperature**, followed by annealing to 300 degrees Celsius. This is **not a stated photoemission measurement temperature**. Instrumental energy/momentum resolution was not established from the inspected main text.

The discussion explicitly explains the minority photohole channel as coupling **predominantly to renormalized Stoner excitations**, opposite in spin transfer to the usual magnon branch. A strong spin-excitation resonance around 0.7 eV and a majority-state feature enter the GT self-energy. The kink energy is not itself a magnon frequency. Bulk LSWT-only EMC cannot be declared a quantitative reproduction of this anomaly.

The data-availability statement supplies the generated/analyzed data **from the corresponding author on reasonable request**. The inspected page does not provide a raw measured dispersion array. No author was contacted and no curve coordinates were fabricated.

## Actual calculation and qualitative visualization

New files are owned by the separate paper repository under `data/bccfe_spectrum_baseline/`:

- `bands_and_reference_bias.pdf/png`: raw paired-spin bands and option-B reference on **481** high-symmetry-path points, with the H|P discontinuity preserved.
- `bare_spectral_maps.pdf/png`: raw spin-resolved noninteracting spectral traces on **241** Gamma–H points, -4 to +1 eV, with a **20 meV Lorentzian half-width used solely for display**.
- `experiment_context.pdf/png`: calculated bare [100], kz=0 bands beside the **unchanged original 2019 Fig. 2**. This is explicitly qualitative. Finite-kz sampling, matrix elements, surface/film conditions and correlations are not corrected or fitted.
- `baseline.npz`, `calculate.py`, `provenance.json`, archived reader inputs and actual source-assessment records.

The 2019 figure is [the primary image](https://cdn.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/blobs/348d/6355843/2aa67833f180/41467_2019_8445_Fig2_HTML.jpg). It is reproduced unchanged with author/DOI attribution under the article's [CC BY 4.0 license](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The side-by-side composition is an adaptation; it is not a new measured figure or this project's GT calculation.

Observed checks: interpolated Hermiticity error **8.29e-15 eV**, finite-window spectral integration error **0.00199235 states**, nine-state wide-window weight error **0.00057834 states**, and repeated symmetry-point eigenvalues agree. Archived-input replay reproduces the NPZ, three PDFs and three PNGs **byte-identically**. Figures were visually inspected; duplicate legends and a hidden discontinuity label were corrected.

The maximum difference between sorted raw and option-B band energy sets over the sampled path is **0.522562 eV**; the real-space residual Frobenius norm is **1.370094 eV**. Neither is an EMC mass enhancement, linewidth or experimental kink. The orbital cross-spin gauge remains assumed aligned; EF=12.6256 eV remains script-provenanced, not fitted or independently validated.

## Required comparison protocol

1. Validate the full Hermitian spin-flip retarded self-energy before promoting the existing single-q toy contraction to a material calculation. Keep occupation factors, creation/annihilation channels and normalized q measure explicit.
2. Produce bare/dressed maps for the same frozen reference and separately show raw-reference bias. Avoid interpreting a reference change as interaction renormalization.
3. Establish q/offset/frequency/eta resolution, causality, spectral weights and spin-channel limits independently of any experimental fit.
4. Obtain the actual low-energy experimental cut, resolution and numerical peak data. Compare spin-resolved peak dispersion and widths, not bare spectral intensity against matrix-element-weighted ARPES intensity.
5. Treat the approximately 40 meV phonon feature, surface optical branch and deep Stoner-driven anomaly as distinct physics. Missing contributions or data are findings, not permission to tune the EMC model.

Material implementation is governed by the [draft PRD](../prd.md); its approval does not imply that experimental agreement has already been obtained.

The reachable electronic baseline and experimental-source comparison are recorded in the [ARPES memo](2026-10-02-bccfe-arpes-comparison.md). The new PRD preserves the old datasets, the eight observed source vetoes, and the distinction between an eligible pilot and a converged material prediction.
