# Native nonorthogonal atomic-orbital electron-magnon coupling

## Problem statement

The current EMC runtime accepts only orthogonal Wannier Hamiltonians.
SIESTA and ABACUS already expose native local-orbital Hamiltonians and
overlaps through HamiltonIO, but dropping the overlap or relabelling a
native model as orthogonal gives incorrect state normalization,
propagation and spectral weights.

The [research memo](../../electron-magnon-coupling-standalone-emc-package-paper/specs/research/2026-10-11-nonorthogonal-emc.md)
establishes the covariant-operator/dual-Green convention and exercises
real readers. It also separates metric correctness from the physical
definition of a local spin perturbation. This PRD proposes a new extension;
it does not retroactively change the existing orthogonal PRD or approve
implementation. Architecture and Stories follow only after approval.

## Goals

- Calculate angle- and boson-normalized electron–magnon vertices from
  native nonorthogonal HamiltonIO models without Wannierization.
- Support both collinear SIESTA and ABACUS inputs with a shared native
  generalized-pencil route and unchanged FM magnon normalization.
- Produce metric-correct electronic self-energies and spin-resolved
  spectral observables using the existing physical channel conventions.
- Make the onsite magnetic-field approximation and its discarded
  nonlocal spin dependence visible in every result.
- Preserve the existing orthogonal consumer behavior and certification.

## Baseline physical scope proposed for approval

Use a fixed spatial AO basis, scalar-relativistic collinear references,
and the existing option-B type local-field model. Form native spin-average
H(R), retain the complete S(R), and keep the magnetic sites' onsite
half-splitting blocks. Report rather than reintroduce discarded nonlocal
and unassigned-site spin-dependent terms.

Independent onsite field tilts perturb the declared covariant magnetic
operator, not the whole H,S basis representation. Their overlap
derivative is zero. This is a model of frozen local fields, not a claim
that the full DFT field response is exactly onsite.

TB2J exchange and moment inputs must record their physical source and
local-field convention. Reusing an exchange file from a different
electronic source is not sufficient evidence of material consistency.
Existing source/mode eligibility checks remain binding.

## Non-goals

- Full real-space exchange-field or Hubbard response export from DFT.
- Screened self-consistent local spin response or new DFT calculations.
- Moving-orbital, phonon, Pulay or spin-lattice overlap derivatives.
- SOC, noncollinear-reference certification, AFM/anomalous-mode extension,
  or a change to the existing magnon normalization.
- PW-projected spectral input, PAW/ultrasoft metric unification,
  Tikhonov/SVD regularization or an implicit pseudoinverse.
- New GPU kernels, performance targets or claims of material convergence.
- Automatic replacement of vetoed sources or relaxation of physical gates.

## Functional requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| FR-001 | Load or accept native collinear HamiltonIO models for both SIESTA and ABACUS. Preserve H(R), S(R), R ordering, atom/orbital ownership, basis/spin order, units, Bloch convention and energy zero; require compatible up/down spatial bases and overlaps. | must |
| FR-002 | Construct the declared native onsite-field reference and report discarded nonlocal/unassigned-site spin dependence. Preserve input models and their complete overlap rather than treating S as identity. | must |
| FR-003 | Solve the generalized electronic eigenproblem at k and k+q. Validate Hermiticity, positive-definite overlap, recorded conditioning and overlap normalization; reject inputs that cannot support the declared precision instead of silently filtering them. | must |
| FR-004 | Construct covariant angle-basis perturbations and project them between normalized expansion coefficients, with no extra overlap in the band vertex. Preserve existing FM boson conversion, site/cell phases, degeneracy treatment and reverse-q adjoint pairing. | must |
| FR-005 | Keep fixed-basis field perturbations distinct from representation changes. Validate finite-angle field-only differences and global rotation covariance with the metric retained. | must |
| FR-006 | Reuse the pinned absorption/emission occupations, denominators and reverse-gauge transport in canonical band space. AO self-energy conversions, when used, must follow the covariant/dual convention. | must |
| FR-007 | Produce native metric-correct Dyson and spin-resolved spectral observables: frequency/chemical-potential/broadening multiply S, physical traces use covariant observables, and finite-window sum-rule residuals remain visible. | must |
| FR-008 | Expose the native route through supported EMC consumer operations, with complete basis/operator/metric provenance and the same fail-closed scientific outcomes as the orthogonal route. Document unsupported spin/basis combinations explicitly. | must |
| FR-009 | Preserve the existing orthogonal path as the S=I limit, including certification, physical output meanings and available execution backends. No flag-only bypass of nonorthogonal validation. | must |
| FR-010 | Exercise both native readers on real Fe fixtures; additionally run an end-to-end certified nonorthogonal model from local reference/magnons through vertex, self-energy and spectrum. A real material spectrum requires independently eligible matched magnetic input. | must |
| FR-011 | Provide usage documentation and a reproducible native-LCAO example with explicit model approximation, source eligibility and unresolved convergence limitations. | must |
| FR-012 | Report gauge-invariant group transition weights and canonical-band spectral quantities in addition to physical spin traces where already supported. Do not introduce an unqualified positive site-population interpretation. | should |

## Non-functional requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| NFR-001 | Reuse HamiltonIO native reader/pencil capabilities; do not create a second parser or independent TB model implementation inside EMC. | must |
| NFR-002 | Pin the electronic metric extension in an approved executable exact derivation/report, using complex nonorthogonal cases and two distinct endpoint metrics. Existing TB2J magnon/spin-normalization derivations remain authoritative. | must |
| NFR-003 | Numerical acceptance must distinguish conditioning and native file precision from exact identities. Architecture must define scale-aware residual thresholds; the recorded SIESTA 1.30e-10 resolvent discrepancy must not be hidden by relabelling it as a 1e-10 pass. | must |
| NFR-004 | Retain bounded k/frequency execution and explicit host/device resource accounting. No all-k overlap inverses or all-q vertices may be retained merely to simplify the native route. | must |
| NFR-005 | Inputs remain immutable during calculation. Result identity includes overlap and the local-operator approximation so incompatible data cannot share certificates or cached preparation. | must |
| NFR-006 | Verification is deterministic, isolated and exercises consumer-visible physics/metrics. Real fixture smokes do not require rerunning DFT or weakening existing full-suite assumptions. | must |

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC-01 — Native readers:** both SIESTA and ABACUS produce consistent
  collinear H,S and normalized eigenpairs at Gamma and a generic k point.
  Record basis size, minimum overlap eigenvalue, condition number,
  Hermiticity and eigenpair/normalization residuals.
- [ ] **AC-02 — Exact metric algebra:** exact complex cases establish the
  native dual resolvent, band projection and self-energy covariance.
  Negative controls fail for an extra inverse metric in the band vertex
  and a naive AO total spectral trace.
- [ ] **AC-03 — Two-mesh invariance:** the same physical band coupling
  agrees under separate nonsingular AO changes at k and k+q, consistent
  metric orthogonalization, and allowed eigenstate-gauge transformations.
- [ ] **AC-04 — Physical perturbation:** a nonorthogonal multisite model
  agrees with independent frozen-field finite-angle differences, obeys
  reverse-q adjoints and preserves the generalized electronic spectrum
  under a global spin rotation. A whole-basis gauge change is not accepted
  as the field-only oracle.
- [ ] **AC-05 — Honest locality:** a fixture with deliberately nonlocal
  spin splitting reports the discarded residue and evaluates the stated
  onsite reference, not a silently substituted full-field derivative.
- [ ] **AC-06 — Spectral observables:** certified nonorthogonal model
  spectra satisfy causality/positivity in physical observables, agree
  with an independent consistently orthogonalized representation, and
  show the correct metric-weighted completeness with reported
  finite-window residuals.
- [ ] **AC-07 — End to end:** a supported native-model consumer scenario
  produces certified vertices, self-energy and spin spectra with
  provenance. Real-reader smokes cover both codes; real material results
  are emitted only for eligible matched exchange/moment sources, with
  rejection evidence otherwise.
- [ ] **AC-08 — Fail closed:** incompatible spin bases/overlaps, singular
  or precision-incompatible metrics, inconsistent provenance and
  unsupported physical modes yield explicit failures rather than
  orthogonal fallback, clipping, filtering or fabricated output.
- [ ] **AC-09 — Orthogonal regression:** S=I reproduces the existing
  physical results and the established orthogonal consumer suite stays
  compatible; documentation distinguishes the two input routes.

## Open questions for architecture after PRD approval

- Which existing public EMC operation should own a loaded native
  HamiltonIO model versus a source-path reader?
- Which provenance establishes compatibility between onsite reference,
  TB2J exchange and moment conventions for the first real-material case?
- Which precision/conditioning policy matches both observed native
  formats without concealing a defective metric?
- Which electronic identities belong in shared mathdocs versus the
  existing package derivation/report layout?

# Native EMC interface and numerical-policy research

## Authority and decision

This is bounded design research under the [approved native PRD](../prd.md), not a canonical Architecture record or implementation approval. Canonical Architecture creation remains gated by the legacy catalog migration. The source/math findings come from [dual-basis research](../../../electron-magnon-coupling-standalone-emc-package-paper/specs/research/2026-10-11-nonorthogonal-emc.md) and the existing [normalization contract](../../../../notes/magnon-vertex-normalization.md).

Recommended design: native H,S readers feed a private electronic-pencil seam; existing certified vertex and canonical-band contraction interfaces remain the scientific core. Do not turn a native input into a purported Wannier model or add a second parser. Decisions below are proposals for the future Architecture gate.

## Vocabulary and invariants

- **Electronic pencil:** the frozen H(k),S(k) pair, its basis/order/Fourier convention and checked generalized eigenstates. S=I is the orthogonal special case, not a separate physical approximation.
- **Covariant perturbation:** the matrix of the declared physical field operator between primal AO basis functions. It is not an inverse-metric-dressed action matrix.
- **Expansion coefficients:** generalized eigenvector columns normalized with S. They differ from primal PW projection amplitudes.
- **Canonical band basis:** normalized physical electron eigenstates; existing retarded spin-flip contractions act in this basis.
- **Onsite-field reference:** retained native spin-average hopping and full overlap, plus selected onsite half-splittings. It is the approved approximate reference model, not the original full DFT field response.
- **Physical certificate:** checks the declared reference and perturbation on stated samples; it does not certify material convergence or compatibility of an arbitrary imported J dataset.

Spin labels are orbital channels, not alternating band labels. Magnetic spin normalization and electronic overlap are distinct quantities. Complete basis dimensions, atom ownership and positive-definite metric are checked explicitly.

## Proposed public consumer interface

Add a native loaded-model factory, tentatively `load_native_inputs(model_up, model_down, tb2j_path, site_orbitals, qpoints, *, provenance, metric_policy)`. It accepts HamiltonIO models, not a new loosely specified H/S dictionary. The caller uses the existing SIESTA or ABACUS parser; package documentation supplies exact reader examples. Both factories return the loaded-input concept consumed by existing `compute_vertex`, `export_vertex`, `certify` and `magnon_spectral` operations. `self_energy` remains a downstream consumer of the resulting certified absorption and reverse-annihilation vertices; it does not accept loaded inputs or bypass the certificate/pair barrier.

Keep `load_inputs` as the supported Wannier90 source factory with its existing call shape. Its orthogonality check must not be weakened to accept unconverted native arrays. Generalize internal loaded/reference typing, not by exposing a false `is_orthogonal` flag.

A native model-to-spectrum facade should reuse the case/cut controls, bounded spectral reducer, writer and physical outcomes of `material_spectrum`. It needs an explicit loaded-native-input entry, not temporary fake Wannier files. Source preflight, provenance and physical spin observables differ; request normalization and canonical-band contraction do not. Architecture must pin the exact public request/report shape after reference checks; no renamed public Fe-only types or compatibility aliases are proposed in this memo.

Source evidence: `emc/loaders.py:14–20,23–86`, `emc/__init__.py:3–39`, `emc/material_spectrum.py:148–304,1576–1668` and `emc/selfenergy.py:11–45`.

## Proposed private module seam

Use one private electronic module, with two concrete adapters: the existing orthogonal Wannier representation and the native HamiltonIO LCAO representation. Keep reader-specific file handling in HamiltonIO. The seam owns:

1. Pencil evaluation and checked state solves on one bounded k block.
2. Projection of covariant operators between the two solved meshes.
3. Physical eigenbasis alignment at a shared momentum and AO gauge.
4. Physical spin-observable matrices in canonical bands.
5. Frozen identity and small numerical diagnostic records.

Do not expose a general plugin system, basis-rotation framework or public cache-lifetime protocol. The adapters genuinely differ in pencil construction, metric, source phase and diagnostics; their downstream canonical-band arrays have the same meaning.

The native adapter uses HamiltonIO's real-space Fourier convention and generalized solve. Assemble the declared interleaved spinor reference once without mutating either input spin model. Preserve all S(R), atom/site mapping and raw spin-average blocks; report discarded spin-dependent blocks. Keep the existing Wannier Wigner–Seitz behavior unchanged.

Native reference identity must include S(R), its R ordering, atom/orbital/spin ordering, native Bloch convention, retained local fields, discarded-field policy, numerical policy and source hashes. Exchange/moment/mode identity remains separate. Cached states never survive changes to either identity.

Source evidence: `HamiltonIO/HamiltonIO/lcao_hamiltonian.py:161–242`, native SIESTA/ABACUS readers, `emc/_preparation.py:46–62,136–158` and `emc/_transitions.py:376–395`.

## Three metric-sensitive operations must not be conflated

**Band vertex.** Project the covariant operator between overlap-normalized expansion coefficients. No additional overlap belongs in this contraction.

**Reverse-emission gauge transport.** At the shared external momentum, alignment uses the metric-weighted overlap of reverse-final and absorption-initial expansion coefficients. The current Euclidean overlap in `_transitions._mint_pair` is not valid for a native AO basis. The existing bare-energy transport and unitarity checks remain; they act on the correctly constructed canonical alignment. Reciprocal-image/Bloch-gauge handling must occur before this overlap is compared.

**Spin observable.** Construct the covariant physical spin operator using the spatial overlap. Its canonical-band matrix, not the naive Euclidean AO projector, enters spin traces. For interleaved collinear data, use the appropriate spin subblocks directly rather than allocate a full identity/projector solely for multiplication.

These corrections are mathematically different: inserting a metric in the vertex would be an error even though it is needed in physical coefficient-space overlaps and observables. A read-only exact complex check on 2026-10-12 showed that metric reverse-basis alignment is unitary while Euclidean coefficient overlap fails for the same physical eigenstates.

Source evidence: `emc/vertex.py:90–138`, `emc/_transitions.py:159–162,192–211`, `emc/material_spectrum.py:691–726` and [the recorded check](../../../../log/electron-magnon-coupling-2026-10-12-nonorthogonal-approval.md).

## Spectral execution and residency

Keep the self-energy and Dyson work in the canonical external-band basis. Construct native AO self-energy/Green matrices only when requested for verification or a retained output. Scalar broadening there multiplies S; physical AO spectral traces include the covariant observable.

Metric validation and diagonalization are CPU work. This feature does not change available orthogonal execution backends or introduce a native GPU eigensolver. Reuse canonical-band contractions only when their existing input contract is met; do not bypass certification by supplying an unchecked g array.

Retain one base-state set plus the active shifted set/block. Borrow shared frozen source/reference arrays. Overlaps needed for reverse alignment and spin observables belong to the bounded external block, not to independent copies for every q certificate. Include their residency in the planner. Never construct all-k explicit S inverses for convenience.

The finite-angle oracle rotates declared fields only, with fixed S. It must independently construct the field change; it cannot call the analytic tangent and echo it. Global spin rotation preserves the generalized spectrum but need not make the transverse Hamiltonian vertex vanish. Existing absorption/emission weights, reverse-mesh proofs and Goldstone exclusions remain unchanged.

## Proposed numerical policy for Architecture review

Record every tolerance in output identity/provenance and apply it at every consumed k point, not just the source smoke sample.

- Reject nonfinite matrices, inconsistent spin bases/R supports and singular or nonpositive S. No implicit pseudoinverse, diagonal shift or spectral filter.
- Proposed float64 defaults: relative H/S Hermiticity defect <=1e-9, scaled generalized-eigenpair residual <=1e-9, normalized C†SC-I residual <=1e-9 and S condition number <=1e8.
- The condition-number ceiling is a rejection policy, not a proof that every observable has eight digits. Each eigensystem still has independent observed residual checks. Do not relax existing physical certification or 5 meV/5% scientific comparison thresholds to satisfy this policy.
- Native-inverse versus spectral-resolvent comparison is an independent diagnostic with proposed relative tolerance 1e-8 at declared complex energies. It is not an excuse to ignore H/S defects. The measured SIESTA 1.30e-10 difference exceeded the earlier exploratory 1e-10 threshold and remains recorded as such.
- Do not silently symmetrize bad inputs before validation. Tiny accepted file-rounding defects are reported; any Hermitian reconstruction used by a solver must have an explicit recorded convention, with a check against the original pencil.
- Architecture review must reconcile these proposed defaults with the two real fixtures, exact algebra and adversarial near-dependent metrics. This memo does not implement or claim those new thresholds passed a production gate.

The observed ABACUS condition number near 1e5 is compatible with this proposed limit, but sampled checks do not establish BZ-wide conditioning. Ill-conditioned metrics must not be hidden by increasing the limit automatically.

## Acceptance coverage and verification order

| PRD criterion | Proposed proof |
|---|---|
| AC-01 native readers | SIESTA and ABACUS real collinear fixtures, both spins, Gamma and generic k; dimensions, S eigenvalues/conditioning and residuals recorded. |
| AC-02 exact algebra | Complex exact derivation: native resolvent, covariant band projection and AO self-energy covariance; negative extra-metric and naive-trace controls. |
| AC-03 two-mesh invariance | Independent nonsingular AO changes at both endpoints, consistent metric orthogonalization and degenerate-band gauge totals. |
| AC-04 physical perturbation | Fixed-S multisite finite-angle oracle, global generalized-spectrum covariance and reverse-q pairing; separate whole-basis gauge negative control. |
| AC-05 locality | Deliberate offsite/unassigned-site spin splitting yields the declared reference and an observable residue record. |
| AC-06 spectra | Canonical-band and independently transformed representation agree; causal PSD physical spin traces and metric completeness with finite-window residuals. |
| AC-07 end to end | Supported loaded-native consumer scenario reaches certified vertex/self-energy/spectrum; both readers exercised separately; material output remains gated by eligible matched magnetic input. |
| AC-08 failures | Incompatible bases/provenance, nonpositive or precision-incompatible S and unsupported modes fail explicitly. |
| AC-09 orthogonal regression | S=I agrees with existing physical results; all affected established consumers and execution backends retain their meaning. |

Implementation should begin with an approved electronic metric derivation/report, then the reference/pencil seam, then certificate and reverse-transport integration, then spectral consumer integration. This is verification order, not an approved Epic/Story set. Mathdocs should own reusable electronic identities; TB2J's existing scripts continue to own magnon/spin normalization. No duplicate authoritative derivation is created by this research.
